item.description: Sit & Stitch is offered the 2nd & 4th Mondays a month from 3:30 to 5:30 pm. For July, it will be the 13th & the 27th. You can drop in for any amount of time. You may continue needle felting and macrame as we now have all of the supplies. We also have some people learning how to knit and crochet. We will also have tea, so bring your favorite covered drink container. Sit and Stitch is for people to come and work on any fiber arts activity that they have while visiting with others. Most people will bring their own projects, but we always have hooks, needles, and yarn and sometimes we will offer a project with instructions that people may choose to make. Let us know what you would like to learn this year. We share ideas, skills, and encouragement with each other. This summer we will be adding sewing, weaving, and decorative mending to our regular projects of knitting and crocheting. Soon, we will also have a sewing machine available for use. item.description:

• Learn the fundamentals of reverse appliqué through layering, stitching, and cutting techniques

*All materials included. No sewing experience required. You're welcome to bring two contrasting T-shirts to incorporate into your project.*

item.title: Another Trip Around the Sun: An Evening of Grateful Dead & Jam Band Magic — Fri Aug 21, 6:00 PM — Sebastopol Community Cultural Center
item.description:
An Evening of Grateful Dead & Jam Band Magic
Friday, August 21st | Doors 6pm, Music 6:30pm Sebastopol Community Cultural Center, 390 Morris St, Sebastopol, CA
Join us for a cosmic celebration of music and community as Sebastopol Community Cultural Center hosts an unforgettable night of Grateful Dead-inspired jams, featuring an all-star lineup of Bay Area favorites.
Anna Elva brings her dynamic, pulse-driven drumming to the stage, fresh off collaborations with Stu Allen & Mars Hotel and the celebrated 40th Grateful Waltz, where she shared the stage with some of the scene's brightest stars.
Scott Guberman, acclaimed keyboardist known for his work with Phil Lesh and Friends and his deep, soulful command of the Hammond B3, brings decades of Grateful Dead expertise to every note he plays.
Mark Karan, the legendary lead guitarist who anchored Bob Weir & RatDog for over a decade, lends his soulful, blues-infused style and unmistakable guitar voodoo to the night's performance.
JP McLean

item.title: The Art of Kokedama: Japanese Moss Ball Planting — Sat Aug 22, 4:00 PM — Gather Sebastopol
item.description:
*With Cathrina of Cat Hawk Gardens, “The Kokedama Mama”*
Discover the Japanese art of kokedama—living plant arrangements wrapped in moss. Guided by Cathrina of Cat Hawk Gardens, you’ll explore this mindful practice of balance, beauty, and simplicity while creating your own kokedama to take home.
**In this workshop you’ll:**
• Learn traditional techniques for forming and binding moss balls
• Make your own kokedama to take home
• Gain skills to continue creating on your own
All supplies provided. Includes a grounding Self-Breema movement practice to connect body and mind.

item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Aug 23, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Sundays in Sonoma at Viansa Winery — Sun Aug 23, 12:00 AM — Viansa Winery
item.description:
Viansa Winery feels made for live music, perched atop the Summit of Sonoma with sweeping vineyard views and Tuscan-inspired charm. This summer and fall, acclaimed singer-songwriter Greg Lamboy brings his warm, intimate sound to the hilltop terrace for select afternoon performances as part of Viansa's outdoor music series. An award-winning guitarist and frontman of the Americana band Pacific Standard, Lamboy is known for pitch-perfect melodies and deeply personal lyrics. His relaxed, soulful style pairs effortlessly with Viansa's panoramic setting, estate wines, and laid-back elegance. Settle in with a tasting, take in the views, and enjoy an afternoon where strong vocals, masterful guitar, and unforgettable songs rise above the everyday. Performance Dates: June 14, June 21, July 12, July 19, July 26, October 4, and October 18 from 12 pm -3 pm.

Have you heard about “Shinrin-yoku” or “forest bathing”? Here is an opportunity to take a walk and experience the practice for yourself. Learn techniques to maximize the health benefits and stress reducing qualities of this walking practice. Shinrin-yoku originated in Japan and is gaining popularity in the United States for its documented health benefits. This practice takes a walk in the woods to another level. A centering and calming restorative practice, it promotes balance and restored vitality through a quality of presence and heightened sensory awareness. Sugarloaf Ridge State Park hosts a Forest Therapy Series as part of its Park Rx Program the 4th Sunday of the month (March through November) led by certified Association of Nature and Forest Therapy (ANFT) practitioners.

item.title: Petaluma River History Paddle — Sun Aug 23, 10:00 AM — The Floathouse Petaluma
item.description:
Enjoy a uniquely Petaluma experience on the water. This two-hour, gentle guided kayak tour launches from The Floathouse Petaluma and explores the river that once served as the region's "saltwater highway." Long before roads and railways, the Petaluma River powered San Francisco, the Gold Rush miners, and even global markets with the produce from local farms and industries, supplying everything from eggs to overalls.
Designed and led by a Petaluman, actor and former history teacher this entertaining and enlightening tour brings history to life through storytelling enhanced by costumed actors on shore. You'll hear fascinating stories from the perspectives of long-ago Petalumans—young workers, entrepreneurs, and colorful characters whose daily lives revolved around the river.
